name: Topology from the geometry of position: Euler to Listing
summary: Euler's measurement-free treatments of bridges and polyhedra, Lhuilier's genus correction and Listing's connectivity studies established a geometry of position whose name was fixed in 1847.

name: Seki: resultants, determinants, elimination
summary: Seki Takakazu found resultant and determinant in elimination.

name: Calculus of variations from the brachistochrone
summary: The brachistochrone challenge and the Bernoullis' isoperimetric problems led Euler to a general variational method and Lagrange to an analytic version with the delta symbol.

name: Trigonometry and the exponential: Cotes, De Moivre, Euler
summary: Bernoulli related inverse sine to logarithm, Cotes and De Moivre linked angle to complex logarithm, and Euler gave exp(ix) = cos x + i sin x.

name: De Moivre's formula: trigonometry and complex powers
summary: Powers of cos x + i sin x tie multiple-angle trigonometry to complex arithmetic.

name: Bernoulli Ars Conjectandi
summary: Bernoulli proved the first law of large numbers.

name: Taylor: finite differences and Taylor's theorem
summary: A treatise created the calculus of finite differences and gave the series later called Taylor's.

name: Euler: complex logarithms and exponentials
summary: Trigonometric and exponential functions were linked through complex arguments and logarithms of negatives.

name: Euler: geodesics from mechanics
summary: Euler derived the geodesic equation for motion on a surface.

name: Clairaut: curves in space
summary: Analytic geometry and calculus were used to study curves of double curvature.
